OPENER · WHAT WE ACTUALLY NEED
Requirements, written by the failures
• The model chooses the next step, so unplanned requests work • Code enforces limits, so it can't loop or overspend • Actions as tools: resize, use a photo, generate
• State that every turn can see • Validated output, every time • Per-brand rules and persona, without code changes
That set of responsibilities has a name: an agent harness.

HARNESS · CONCEPT
The agent loop: the model never runs anything itself
An agent harness is everything around the model that makes it reliable. The model proposes; the harness enforces.
1 Build context
2 Model proposes
3 Check the call
4 Run the tool
5 Feed back, loop
6 Stop, validate

HARNESS · CONCEPT · LIMITS
Every limit catches something the others miss
Limit
Catches
Misses
Step cap
Runaway loops
Cuts off long, real work
Nested time limits
Hangs, slow tools
Fast loops that go nowhere
Per-tool breaker
One tool failing again and again
Calls that "succeed" pointlessly
Budget
The 4th image when the budget is 3
Loops that cost nothing
COUNT BY NAME
A stuck model retries with slightly different arguments. Count failures by the tool's name.
WHO STOPS THE LOOP
Agno's tool_call_limit skips extra calls but keeps looping. Our own hook raises StopAgentRun and ends the run. Don't set both: the limit is checked before any hook runs, so call 7 is skipped before step_cap sees it and the run never stops.
Harness
HARNESS · HOW PENCIL DOES IT
One broken tool, fourteen minutes: Pencil chose a breaker, not a step cap
~50
dead tool calls in one turn
~14 min
a search tool that wasn't there
THE BREAKER, PER TOOL NAME
2nd failure → a nudge 3rd → tool disabled for the turn 12th → turn ends (strict mode only)
Gained
Long, legitimate turns aren't cut off by a fixed count
Cost
Calls that succeed but go nowhere run until the 1-hour turn limit

HARNESS · CONCEPT · OUTPUT, STATE AND MODELS
A typed result or a typed error, never "anything"
the form the model must fill
class PosterSpec(BaseModel): headline: str # ≤ 6 words subheadline: str # ≤ 12 words body: str # ≤ 25 words image_prompt: str # picture only
1 · Check the shape (schema)
2 · Check the rules in code
3 · Fails? One repair, with the errors
4 · Fails again? A typed error
At Pencil: the agent ends by naming its final outputs, and later tool calls are refused. A blank answer is retried once on the same model, then shown as an error.
State
Transcript: everything said, stored
Context window: what the model sees this turn, such as the last 5 turns
Session id: set by the harness, never by the request
Models
One interface: ask for "provider:model"
A model per task: fast for copy, strong for planning
Fake models in tests: good, malformed, endless

Every tool needs a leash

model    copy phase · fake:endless · sent 228, got back 75 tool     generate_image("…better sky, try 1") → poster-1.png tool     generate_image("…better sky, try 2") → poster-2.png tool     generate_image("…better sky, try 3") → poster-3.png refused  generate_image: image budget of 3 spent refused  generate_image: image budget of 3 spent refused  generate_image: image budget of 3 spent stop     step cap of 6 tool calls reached, run ended picture  saved data/outputs/poster-3.png
The picture phase only sees the image prompt

3
pictures per request
6
tool calls per run
Who stops the loop?
Agno's tool_call_limit skips the tool and asks the model to stop; a model that does not listen loops forever. Our hook raises StopAgentRun and ends the run. Don't set both: the limit is checked before the hooks, so call 7 never reaches step_cap and the run never stops.

No tool takes a folder name

Keyword search breaks when the words differ
“How do I clean the lid?” returns 5 chunks, none about the lid, though “hand-wash only” is in the guide.
The question
The chunk it should find
Why keywords miss
“How do I clean the lid?”
“The lid is hand-wash only”
Different words, same meaning
“Will it spill in my bag?”
“Leak-proof lid”
Paraphrase
“Warm on a long shift?”
“Hot for 12 hours”
Paraphrase
“Not dishwasher-safe”
“Dishwasher-safe”
Negation scores the same
Where keywords still win: exact names and numbers, such as “Tidal” or “750 ml”.
THE OBVIOUS FIX: A SYNONYM LIST
Add a list of synonyms: “clean” = wash, rinse, dishwasher.
WHAT HAPPENS
“Clean the lid” now works. Then “Will it spill in my bag?” misses “leak-proof”, and “warm on a long shift” misses “hot for 12 hours”. The list never ends.
We need to match what the words mean, not the words themselves.

“clean the lid”

Illustrative. Texts that mean similar things sit close together. Green: questions; navy: chunks.
• An embedding model turns text into a list of numbers that captures its meaning • Embed every chunk once; embed the query each time • Rank chunks by how close they are (cosine similarity)

RAG · D · HOW PENCIL DOES IT
Pencil runs one hybrid, scoped lookup
AT PENCIL
Hybrid lookup: keyword ranking and embedding similarity merged with reciprocal rank fusion, at most 5 results, and a small referee model only when the two disagree.
This is how Scribble finds skills and agents for a request, not how it retrieves brand documents. The design questions are the same.
Gained
• Exact terms and paraphrases both work • One user’s memory store can’t be asked for another user’s notes: scope lives in code, and the prompt line about other users is never the boundary.
Cost
• Every query path has to carry identity • On ties, the referee took most of a 4-second lookup
